title: Starter credits -> Path to prod: quickstart messaging & pricing experiments
content:
Purpose:
This is a working brief for a short, high-conversion developer onramp that uses starter credits as the psychological and economic friction reducer. Aim: produce 2–3 landing variants + 3 onboarding microcopy sets + a concise pricing language draft for the hosted API page and email drip.

Target audience:
- Engineers and ML engineers evaluating an API for rapid prototyping and early production (PLG motion).
- Primary persona: backend engineer who needs to ship a proof-of-concept in <72 hours. Secondary persona: product manager curious about unit economics before committing to Dedicated.

High-level thesis:
Starter credits lower the activation time and remove billing anxiety. Coupled with developer-first quickstarts (30s sandbox + 10-line SDK example + sample app deploy button) we can reduce time-to-first meaningful metric (first token produced + first integration test) from days to minutes. Pricing language should be transparently simple (per-token + embedding units) with a clear path to reserved capacity.

Key developer-first value props (short bullets for hero + feature bullets):
- Get a working response in 30 seconds: deploy a serverless example with a single API key and starter credits.
- Pay only for what you use: linear per-token pricing with an estimator in the console and a developer-visible token breakdown per request.
- Predictable performance: curated model profiles and latency SLAs by tier (DEV / PROD).
- Control costs as you scale: recommendations (batching + cache + quantization) surfaced after first 1k requests.
- Same API across hosted, dedicated, and private — drop-in migration path.

Quickstart angles (three distinct flows to A/B test):
1) 30s Demo Flow (Speed-first): landing CTA "Start in 30s — $20 starter credits" -> browser demo that streams a 1-paragraph generation -> sign up minimal form -> starter credits applied
2) 5-min Integration Flow (Code-first): landing CTA "10 lines to production" -> shows Node/Python snippet with one API call and sample response -> deploy button that creates a small Cloud Run function + applies starter credits
3) Sandbox-to-API Flow (Experiment-first): CTA "Sandbox + Postman collection" -> preloaded sandbox with sample prompts and embeddings tests + downloadable Postman/Insomnia collection -> prompts user to run their first query which consumes credits

Pricing language (drafts to iterate on):
- Short hero line: "Usage-based pricing. Transparent per-token rates, free starter credits to get you to first prototype."
- Microcopy for billing: "Starter credits cover your first prototype — no card required for the free tier. After credits, pay per token (text gen X USD / 1,000 tokens; embeddings Y USD / 1,000 embeddings)."
- Upgrade path: "Teams growing beyond budget? Reserve Dedicated capacity for predictable monthly throughput and volume discounts."
- Cost clarity callout (console): "Estimated cost per request" with sample token breakdown and recommended optimizer (batching/caching).

Competitive positioning notes (quick raw analysis):
- Player A (managed endpoints from hyperscaler): advantage = infra + ecosystem; disadvantage = higher per-unit cost and slower feature rollouts for LLM-specific ergonomics. Message: "Lower latency, model-aware optimizations, and clearer unit economics for inference workloads."
- Player B (LLM API competitor): advantage = brand awareness; disadvantage = less flexible deployment modes and opaque performance. Message: "Same simple API plus a migration path to Dedicated/Private with predictable SLOs."
- Self-host (open-source + infra): advantage = control/cost at scale; disadvantage = build/ops cost, no out-of-the-box batching/caching/kv features. Message: "Skip the ops — get production-grade inference primitives (KV cache, continuous batching) out of the box and start iterating immediately."

Common objections + suggested rebuttals (for sales/DMs/Docs):
- "How do you compare on cost?" -> Provide a sample cost calc for a 5M token/month workload showing Redwood Optimize recommendations and potential 20–40% unit cost reduction vs naive self-hosting once you include ops overhead.
- "What about model choice?" -> We provide a curated catalog and model variants with performance profiles (latency, cost, quality) and automated fallbacks.
- "Is there a free tier?" -> Yes: starter credits (N USD) + low-usage free tier for embeddings under M units/month (experiment to confirm thresholds).

Landing page copy snippets (short variants):
- One-liner A: "Build with a predictably fast LLM API — try $20 starter credits and ship in minutes."
- One-liner B: "From prototype to production: low-latency inference, transparent pricing, and an easy path to Dedicated capacity."
- CTA variants: "Start with credits" / "Try a 30s demo" / "Deploy a sample app"

Email drip subject lines and first-sentence tests (to A/B with starter credits vs no credits):
- Subject A: "$20 credit to build your first LLM feature in 30 minutes" -> First sentence: "We gave you $20 to try Redwood — here’s a 30s demo you can run in your browser."
- Subject B: "10 lines to production: Node + Redwood" -> First sentence: "See how an assistant takes shape with a single API call and starter credits applied automatically."

Onboarding microcopy for console and SDKs (short):
- SDK install page: "Install in one line. Create an API key. Run this example. Watch it stream back tokens."
- Billing card prompt: "Add a billing card when you want to turn on auto-topup. Starter credits last 30 days."
- Cost estimator tooltip: "Estimates are based on model and length; actual usage may vary. Need help? Contact success@redwood.com."

Measurement plan (what we track during experiment):
- Activation funnel: page view -> sign up -> first token returned (target: 50% within 1 hour)
- Time to first meaningful action (demo run or deployed sample)
- TTR (token-to-request) and avg tokens per session during starter credits window
- Conversion to paid within 30 days and usage tiers after credits expire
- Support contacts and common friction points logged in Intercom

Quick experiments & hypotheses (two-week sprints):
- H1: Adding $20 starter credits increases time-to-first-token completion by +40% and increases 30-day paid conversion by +15% among self-serve signups. Test: cohort A (credits + 30s demo) vs cohort B (demo only).
- H2: A 10-line Node quickstart with a deploy button increases developer-to-deployed-sample rate by 2x compared to copy-only quickstart.

Next steps and open questions (TODOs):
- Validate starter credit amount: $10 vs $20 vs $50. Finance sign-off required for chosen amount and fraud controls (GT-412).
- Developer UX: finalize the 30s browser demo UX and decide whether it runs on shared sandbox infra or ephemeral customer sandbox.
- Console work: Add "estimated cost per request" widget (small UX spike).
- Content: produce 2 landing hero variants and 3 email templates; link to GH PR for copy review (see linked_artifacts).

Notes / links to internal threads and artifacts:
- Slack thread: #gt-hosted-api-onramp (search: "starter credits experiment")
- PR for quickstart infra: https://github.com/redwood-inference/demo-deploy/pull/37
- Finance ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/FIN-89 (fraud guard and credits accounting)

Rough timeline (recommended):
- Week 0: finalize credit amount and landing copy -> produce two hero variants
- Week 1: build 30s demo + 10-line quickstart + deploy button -> internal dogfood
- Week 2: soft launch to 5k visits (paid acquisition and organic channels) -> measure funnel
- Week 4: iterate on top funnel blockers and begin dedicated upsell experiments

Appendix: sample quickstart (for engineering to polish)
- Node example (10 lines): const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference'); const c = new Redwood({key: process.env.RW_KEY}); const r = await c.text.generate({model:'rwd-small-v1',input:'Summarize:...'}); console.log(r.text);

End of draft.

Author notes: prefer short, concrete CTAs and remove fluff. Focus A/B tests on friction removal (starter credits + runnable demo) rather than small copy tweaks. This doc will be iterated in product/marketing reviews.
